findings.evidence: Section §1.5 Common Mistakes: "Ignoring the input/output asymmetry. Treating a request as 'one unit' hides that input-heavy workloads tend toward high prefill compute and KV-capacity pressure, while output-heavy ones are decode-dominant (run-time per generated token) — opposite bottlenecks with opposite fixes." The parenthetical "(run-time per generated token)" glosses "decode-dominant" but introduces a third name ("run-time") that does not appear in the book's defined terminology elsewhere, where decode is consistently described as "bandwidth-bound" or by TPOT.
findings.issue: The phrase 'run-time per generated token' introduces an ad-hoc synonym for decode cost that conflicts with the book's established terminology (TPOT, decode bandwidth-bound). A reader tracing this term elsewhere will not find it defined.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace '(run-time per generated token)' with the book's standard term, e.g. '(TPOT × output length)' or '(per-token decode cost)'.

findings.evidence: "[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] — the schematic is drawn from the documented mechanism ([1P][FACT]: the per-token K/V accounting of the DeepSeek-V2 MLA report, arXiv:2405.04434), and the 64-head geometry it abbreviates carries that same label ([canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], Ch. 4, Table 4-2), not a vendor checkpoint"
findings.issue: Ambiguous, self-contradictory label referent: 'that same label' grammatically points to the figure's own [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] tag, but the parenthetical assigns [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION] — two different Axis-1 provenances under the book's own taxonomy (Table 4-2 Note 1: '[canonical scenario] is distinct from [ILLUSTRATIVE]'). The reader cannot determine which label the 64-head geometry actually carries.
findings.fix_instruction: Reword to '...and the 64-head geometry it abbreviates carries its own label ([canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION], Ch. 4, Table 4-2)' so the figure tag and the geometry tag are no longer conflated by 'that same label'.

findings.chapter: Ch 1 §1.1.2 / Ch 3 §3.6.1 vs Preface cross-reference convention (printed p. xix)
findings.evidence: Preface convention: "Appendix A numbers its own sections with a letter suffix, so Appendix A § 9A means Appendix A, the section labelled 9A; the appendix's figures carry A.N." Ch 1 (printed p. 3): "...all accessed 2026-08-30, the book's evidence cutoff; Appendix A §10". Ch 3 (printed p. 51): "(source: model card HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, accessed 2026-08-30; A.10)".
findings.issue: Three mutually inconsistent forms for appendix pointers: the stated convention (letter-suffixed sections, e.g. §9A; figures A.N), an unsuffixed 'Appendix A §10', and a bare 'A.10' that collides with the appendix's figure-numbering form (List of Figures shows only A.1–A.5, so 'A.10' cannot be a figure and is not a well-formed section reference either). At least one of the three is wrong, and the targets cannot be confirmed to resolve.
findings.fix_instruction: Adopt one section form (e.g. 'Appendix A §10A' or, if unsuffixed sections exist, 'Appendix A §10'), amend the Preface convention sentence accordingly, and replace the bare 'A.10' on printed p. 51 with the full section form.
